claims.text: The as-cast rare-earth-free high-entropy alloy has a naturally occurring nanoscale multiphase microstructure with compositional fluctuations and defined phase boundaries.
Controlled annealing modifies the nanoscale distribution of compositional inhomogeneities.
Nanoscale compositional heterogeneities and phase boundaries locally mediate magnetic order.
Nanoscale compositional heterogeneities and phase boundaries facilitate efficient thermal conduction.
Controlled heat treatment refines the nanoscale microstructure.
The refined microstructure creates regions whose magnetic ordering can reorient readily under low external fields.
Microstructural tuning lowers the energy barriers for local magnetostructural transitions.
Lower barriers for local magnetostructural transitions enhance the low-field magnetocaloric effect.
Heat-treatment-induced microstructural tuning minimizes domain-wall pinning.
Minimized domain-wall pinning reduces magnetic hysteresis.
The proposed microstructural tuning preserves rapid heat exchange.
The proposed microstructural tuning preserves mechanical integrity.
Relative to the as-cast alloy, the heat-treated alloy will show a larger low-field isothermal entropy change.
Relative to the as-cast alloy, the heat-treated alloy will show reduced magnetic hysteresis.
Relative to the as-cast alloy, the heat-treated alloy will maintain rapid heat exchange.
Relative to the as-cast alloy, the heat-treated alloy will maintain mechanical stability.
The proposed relationships are expected to hold near the magnetic transition and near room temperature at applied fields below approximately 1 T.
The applicability of the hypothesis at very high fields or temperatures far from the magnetic transition is uncertain.
The general trend of enhanced magnetocaloric performance through nanoscale tuning is supported by prior knowledge.
The magnitude of improvement and its sensitivity to specific heat-treatment parameters remain uncertain.
